module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Gourevitch's series identity

*References:*
 - [About a New Kind of Ramanujan-Type Series](https://doi.org/10.1080/10586458.2003.10504518) by *Jesús Guillera*
 - [G2003] Guillera, Jesús. "About a new kind of Ramanujan-type series." Experimental Mathematics 12.4 (2003): 507-510.
 - [A2025] Au, Kam Cheong. "Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities." Journal of Symbolic Computation 130 (2025): 102421. [arXiv:2312.14051](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14051)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Gourevitch


/-- The Gourevitch series identity:
The following identity holds:
$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{1 + 14 n + 76 n^2 + 168 n^3}{2^{20 n}} \binom{2n}{n}^7 = \frac{32}{\pi^3}.$
This was originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera and proven in [A2025] by Au.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem gourevitch_series_identity :
    ∑' n : ℕ, ((1 + 14 * n + 76 * n ^ 2 + 168 * n ^ 3) / (2 ^ (20 * n)) : ℝ)
      * Nat.centralBinom n ^ 7 = 32 / (Real.pi ^ 3) := by
  sorry

end Gourevitch

findings.description: The theorem docstring says the identity "was originally conjectured in [G2003] by Guillera". The identity was actually found empirically, with PSLQ, by Boris Gourevitch in 2002 and sent privately to Guillera, who first published it in [G2003]. The file's own title ("Gourevitch's series identity") has the attribution right. The mathematics is unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: [G2003]'s own reference list (Crossref metadata, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/10586458.2003.10504518) cites "Gourevitch, B. 2002. [Gourevitch 02], Personal communication". Guillera, 'History of the formulas and algorithms for pi' (arXiv:0807.0872): "B. Gourevitch found a series for 1/π^3 \cite{guillera3} [= About a new kind of Ramanujan type series, Exp. Math. 12 (2003)] using the PSLQ algorithm ... It has not been proved yet." Guillera's homepage (https://anamat.unizar.es/jguillera/samples.html): "In 2023 Kam Cheong Au gave a proof of the Ramanujan-like series for 1/π^3 conjectured by Boris Gourevitch." Cohen–Guillera (arXiv:2101.12592): "the formula for 1/π^3 was found by B. Gourevitch". Au (arXiv:2312.14051): "due to B. Gourevich".
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring to: "This identity was found empirically by B. Gourevitch and first published, as a conjecture, in [G2003] by Guillera. It was proven in [A2025] by Au."

reformulations.difference: The Lean term is binomial: (1+14n+76n^2+168n^3)/2^(20n) · centralBinom(n)^7. The proving paper (Au, arXiv:2312.14051) uses Pochhammer form: Σ (1/2)_n^7/(1)_n^7 · 2^(-6n) · (168n^3+76n^2+14n+1). A reader comparing the two might take 2^(20n) vs 2^(6n) for an error.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1/2)_n/n! = C(2n,n)/4^n. By induction this uses (n+1)·C(2n+2,n+1) = 2(2n+1)·C(2n,n) (Mathlib `Nat.succ_mul_centralBinom_succ`). So (1/2)_n^7/(1)_n^7 · 2^(-6n) = C(2n,n)^7 · 2^(-14n) · 2^(-6n) = C(2n,n)^7 · 2^(-20n). The summands agree for every n, so the two tsum identities are the same statement. Guillera's own restatement of [G2003] (arXiv:0807.0872) uses the binomial form, (2n)!^7/n!^14 · 2^(-20n). I proved the ↔ in Lean via termwise `simp_rw`.

sources_consulted: arXiv e-print 2312.14051 (LaTeX source of Au, 'Wilf-Zeilberger seeds and non-trivial hypergeometric identities': intro display and Example ex_pi-3)
arXiv e-print 0807.0872 (Guillera, 'History of the formulas and algorithms for pi', section 'Very recent results')
arXiv e-print 2101.12592 (Cohen & Guillera, 'Rational Hypergeometric Ramanujan Identities for 1/π^c: Survey and Generalizations', table of 1/π^c formulas, entry #11)

review.notes:
The single theorem states the source's identity faithfully. Checks in /workspace/review:
(1) With pp.all, the statement elaborates entirely in ℝ: (1 + 14·↑n + 76·↑n^2 + 168·↑n^3) / (2:ℝ)^(20·n) · (↑(centralBinom n))^7, with an unconditional tsum. Nat.centralBinom n = (2n).choose n.
(2) I proved the series `Summable` in Lean, bounding each term by (259 n^3 + 1)/64^n via centralBinom_le_four_pow. So `∑'` is the genuine sum, not the junk value 0.
(3) Exact ℚ partial sums: S_30 agrees with 32/π^3 (π to 60 digits) to within 1e-45, i.e. 40+ correct digits. S_20 is off by about 5e-37, consistent with the ratio-1/64 geometric convergence.
(4) I proved in Lean that the statement is equivalent to Au's Pochhammer form.
Status: `research solved` matches the source. Au proved the identity (arXiv:2312.14051, J. Symbolic Comput. 130 (2025) 102421), and Guillera's homepage also reports a simpler 2025 WZ proof. No status issue. I could not read the full text of [G2003] itself (Taylor & Francis and Project Euclid block automated access). The formula as posed there is corroborated by Guillera's own restatement citing [G2003] (arXiv:0807.0872), by the Cohen–Guillera survey, and by Au's paper. The only defect is the minor attribution slip in the docstring: the identity is Gourevitch's, not Guillera's.
